- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrects or lags in mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in high-volatility periods — model reacts too aggressively to short-term noise.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing true price trends — especially when prices are trending downward, forecasts remain elevated.
- When history shows strong mean reversion, model fails to adjust forecast downward sufficiently early — leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model tends to overfit recent high prices, ignoring longer-term mean or seasonal patterns — especially in low-volatility periods.
- Forecast error is more severe when true price moves are large and sudden — model struggles with volatility clustering.
